subject: Proposal: delegated host identity + ephemeral cert workflow for private endpoints
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: delegated host identity + ephemeral cert workflow for private endpoints

Team —

Following the customer workshop with Acme earlier today, I put together a short proposal for how we can handle host identity and short-lived certs for private (VPC/on-prem) endpoints. Goal: give Acme a path to assert ownership of private FQDNs while letting Redwood manage ephemeral TLS for runtime servers with minimal manual handoffs.

Summary (see attached PDF for diagrams):
- Delegated Host Identity: customer proves domain ownership via DNS TXT for a small validation token, then delegates assertion to a tenant-scoped authority in Redwood (no public CA needed).
- Ephemeral leaf certs: issue short-lived (1h–6h) certs from our tenant CA for runtime hosts. Certs are provisioned via CSR signed by a customer escrow key or via Vault-signed CSR (customer choice).
- CSR escrow: when customer wants full custody, they can escrow a CSR template + key into their KMS and give Redwood limited signing rights; alternatively, we sign ephemeral certs ourselves but record full audit trail and provide KMS-wrapped private keys for audits.
- Split-DNS considerations: support split-horizon (private resolver) with a per-tenant zone that points to internal endpoints. Validation flow needs to confirm the TXT token via the resolver the customer designates (not public DNS).

Actionable next steps I propose:
1) Engineering review of validation flow (Hiro). Can we verify TXT via a customer-provided resolver over a short-lived tunnel?
2) Security review of CSR escrow vs. tenant CA model (Kimberly). What are compliance implications (SOC 2) for escrowed keys?
3) Ops runbook + rollout checklist for customers on Dedicated & Private (Marissa).
4) Send this proposal to Acme with choices and recommended default (I recommend tenant CA + auditable key export).

PTLs: Hiro, Kimberly, Marissa — please comment inline by Tue EOD so we can present a refined plan to Acme Wed morning.

Thanks,

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deploys
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- delegated-host-identity-proposal.pdf (diagram + flows)
- csr-escrow-template.txt (example CSR/metadata)
From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 01:35:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Proposal: delegated host identity + ephemeral cert workflow for private endpoints

Hannah —

Good proposal, high level looks fine. A few technical notes / questions:

1) DNS TXT validation over customer resolver: we should avoid shipping a long-lived tunnel. Instead, ask the customer to run a short-lived validation agent (container) that we call via mutual TLS to query their resolver over port 53 inside their VPC — that keeps queries in-plane and avoids exposing tokens externally.

2) Timing and TTLs: if we rely on customer resolver, we need to account for negative caching TTLs. Recommend TTL <= 60s for the validation token and a backoff / retry window of up to 2 minutes. Include explicit rollback steps when tokens are removed.

3) Ephemeral cert churn: 1h certs are fine but we should support a configurable window (default 4h) and provide a metric to show renewal success/failure per-host. Also ensure KV cache of the runtime avoids reusing stale sessions during rotation.

4) OCSP/CRL: for ephemeral certs OCSP check introduces latency; consider OCSP stapling at the proxy we control or short-lived certs without OCSP but with strict audit logs (prefers stapling).

I'll add a rough sequence diagram to the Drive doc.

- Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: delegated host identity + ephemeral cert workflow for private endpoints

All —

Security/compliance POV: two things to consider before we present a recommended default to Acme:

A) CSR escrow model: if customers escrow private keys into their KMS and Redwood performs signing using a delegated role, that is acceptable for SOC 2 provided we: (i) have per-operation audit logs, (ii) can provide proof of nondisclosure (we never export keys), and (iii) periodic attestation that signing roles are limited scope. We must add a contractual clause restricting Redwood from exporting or retaining escrowed keys.

B) Tenant CA model (Redwood-issued ephemeral certs): easier operationally but the customer may require full traceability of private key usage. For regulated customers (finance/healthcare) prefer escrow or HSM-backed key ops with an auditable KMS.

Other notes: require a signed ATO checklist for any customer that chooses escrow. Also include a minimum key-size and enforced automated rotation of CA intermediate keys (rolling window).

I'll draft a short compliance appendix for the Drive doc and add the ATO checklist template.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposal: delegated host identity + ephemeral cert workflow for private endpoints

Thanks for the quick turn on this — useful doc and clear options. A couple of clarifications from Acme: 

1) We prefer the escrowed CSR option (we want control over private keys). Our security team runs keys in AWS KMS, not HSM. Is that sufficient?

2) For TXT validation we can spin up a short-lived validation agent in our prod VPC (container) and expose a local API for Redwood to call over the agreed peering link. Happy with the agent approach Hiro suggested.

3) Can you confirm if Redwood will provide a fallback if our peering link is temporarily down (e.g., a signed long-lived assertion token we can rotate)? We need uninterrupted traffic during maintenance windows.

Next steps for us: we can provision the KMS role and a test VPC agent for Wed. Can you share the ATO checklist and the CSR template so our security team can review?

Appreciate it — Alice
Alice Romero
Sr. Platform Engineer, Acme Corp
